newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks overcome late drop to close higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks overcome late drop to close higher.

text.p: Swiss shares closed near the day's highs in sizeable volumes after a positive Wall Street opening helped the shares overcome a late bout of weakness.

"The outcome of U.S. elections confirmed the markets' high hopes, but we will have to see whether good sentiment will hold very much longer", a dealer said, adding the market was likely to be volatile in the next few days.
Thursday's U.S. economic data and uncertainty over Russian president Yeltsin's condition may lead to a more cautious stance, he added.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended higher by 30.6 points, or 0.81 percent, at 3,815.4 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 16.27 points, or 0.67 percent, to 2,442.86.
Actively-traded Roche, which briefly made losses in late trade, ended up ten francs at 9,760.
Ciba and Sandoz added more than one percent each, profiting in part from from a buy program.
Dollar-sensitive Nestle and SMH gained ground.
Electrowatt gave up recent gains. Electrowatt stocks, which have profited lately from renewed rumours about CS Holding intending to sell its 45 percent stake in the company, lost one franc to 492.
Alusuisse continued to rise on Tuesday's news that finance officer Sergio Marchionne would become CEO next April, adding two Swiss francs to 951.
UBS bearer shares added five francs to 1,227.
SBC saw active interest, rising two francs to 249.75. SBC is due to release nine-month figures early on Thursday.
Insurers generally posted smaller gains. Winterthur fell three francs to 758 after rating agency Moody's said on Tuesday it was considering placing the Aaa-rated insurer under review.
